tasks.short: Create remediation diagrams from checked geometry and presentation rules

steps.what: Choose remediation content and prepare checked geometry, layers, labels and presentation rules
Create diagrams by arranging the specified map views, symbols, scales and legends
Check the diagram communicates the intended remediation and accept the exact version for sharing

tasks.design: Configure reusable diagram layouts in the {OTHER} geospatial mapping and drawing environment from planner-checked geometry and presentation rules. Store the result in {DOCS}; the planner checks graphical meaning against the remediation plan before accepting it for sharing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated view, symbol and legend preparation required manual layout after the diagram's substantive content was determined.
tasks.enabler_now: Native mapping and drawing templates can apply explicit layout rules without inventing remediation geometry.
tasks.still_hard: A geometrically correct diagram can still imply the wrong intervention boundary or conceal important uncertainty.
tasks.human_edge: The planner judges whether the graphic communicates the proposed work faithfully to its intended audience.
tasks.altitude: Repeated layout preparation may fall; diagram content and acceptance remain with the planner.

reach.task: Preserve source geometry and map conventions in a remediation diagram
reach.learn: Coordinate references, scales and graphical uncertainty

evidence.claim: Configured mapping and drawing layouts from checked geometry are a model-knowledge design; no measured remediation diagram saving is supplied by the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is diagram content preparation, layout and acceptance, not choosing the remediation strategy or collecting original survey data. Reused plan-development actions are counted in their original task.

Existing survey and project teams produce source maps and the remediation plan. In fully retained s1 the planner checks geometry version, coordinate reference, intervention boundaries, layer ids, labels, view extents, scale, legend and intended audience.
s2 uses the source package and specification produced in s1. No ready diagram-complete flag is presumed; missing geometry or ambiguous symbols return to manual preparation in s1.

Test native mapping and drawing templates before custom code. OTHER denotes geospatial mapping and drawing software. Existing rendering runtime earns no saving; the change concerns repeated manual layout.
Bespoke illustration without reusable views remains manual. Template maintenance and extra source clarification are explicitly counted.
research_questions: Can native diagram templates reduce repeated layout without increasing boundary or symbol misunderstandings?

already_counted.description: Prepare checked geometry and capture presentation rules
Check graphical meaning and accept the diagram

incremental.description: Maintain diagram templates and source-layer mappings
Geospatial colleagues clarify changed source geometry

approvals.approved_version: Exact diagram version, geometry snapshot, remediation plan version and intended audience verified in s3; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=65; gross 35 minus 7 focal upkeep gives central net 28. Range covers already-configured diagrams and modest repeated-layout reuse; geometry preparation and graphical acceptance remain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Develop site-specific environmental plans for energy infrastructure

steps.what: Assess site ecology, infrastructure constraints and evidence to choose environmental management and restoration measures
Develop the environmental plan document explaining selected measures, monitoring, dependencies and evidence limits

loop.purpose: Draft explanatory plan prose from measures chosen by the planner
loop.input: site management plan brief and its controlled evidence references
loop.output: draft explaining selected measures, constraints, monitoring and unresolved questions
loop.check: Planner checks ecological meaning, infrastructure limitations, timing and that no safety or effectiveness assurance exceeds the evidence
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; conflicting constraints or unsupported measures return to manual planning and writing
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed template cannot explain site-specific environmental reasoning and interacting constraints

steps.what: Verify the plan with infrastructure specialists and accept it for the site's approval process

tasks.design: Draft the plan in {DOCS} from measures and constraints already assessed by the planner with infrastructure specialists. Use the {OTHER} site environmental and asset information environment for source references; the planner accepts the exact document for separate site approval without authorising operational work.
tasks.previous_blocker: Explaining site-specific environmental measures in a coherent plan required prose work after the substantive strategy was selected.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded drafting function can propose wording while preserving traceability to selected measures and evidence.
tasks.still_hard: Restoration objectives can conflict with asset access, operating requirements and uncertain ecological response.
tasks.human_edge: The planner reconciles ecological aims with infrastructure realities and knows which uncertainties require specialist resolution.
tasks.altitude: Some document drafting may fall; environmental strategy, specialist coordination and acceptance remain human.

reach.task: Explain asset constraints affecting restoration and environmental management
reach.learn: Access limits, operational interfaces and controlled work boundaries

evidence.claim: Source-grounded drafting of planner-selected environmental measures is a model-knowledge design; no supplied case measures savings for energy-infrastructure environmental plans.

assumptions: Boundary is environmental strategy and plan writing through planner acceptance, not site authorisation, asset operation or implementation. If this is the same plan action counted in another restoration-planning task, the roll-up assigns it once.

Site ecologists supply existing observations and infrastructure specialists supply asset constraints. In fully retained s1 the planner verifies site and asset identifiers, source versions, chosen measures, timing, monitoring criteria, access assumptions and unresolved risks.

The loop reads that brief directly. No ready safe-access, environmentally acceptable or approved-measure flag is presumed; missing constraints return to manual specialist enquiry in s1 or s3 and manual drafting in s2.
Test native controlled templates and approved drafting functions before custom code. OTHER denotes site environmental and asset information software.
s3 acceptance is not a permit or asset safety authorisation. All technical acceptance remains fully counted, and additional specialist review and drafting upkeep have allowances.
unknowns: Required independent environmental and operational approvals
Permission to process asset information in drafting tools
research_questions: Can reviewed drafts preserve infrastructure constraints and ecological uncertainties without increasing specialist corrections?

already_counted.description: Check and correct environmental plan prose

incremental.description: Maintain plan drafting checks and source references
Infrastructure or ecology specialists resolve additional draft ambiguities

approvals.approved_version: Exact site environmental plan, asset context, selected measures and evidence snapshot checked in s3; changes void planner acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=91; gross 9 minus 6 focal upkeep gives central net 3. Range covers novel sites requiring manual prose and limited document reuse; strategy and specialist acceptance remain full time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Repeated diagram layouts and some plan prose may take less preparation, while ecological decisions and infrastructure coordination remain with the planner.
reach: Work with geospatial analysts on diagram provenance
Learn asset constraints from infrastructure specialists
role.ambitious_version: A planner who communicates restoration proposals clearly while preserving the environmental and operational limits of the evidence.
